problem_markdown: If real $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ satisfy $\sum x_i^2=1$, prove that for each integer $k\ge2$ there are integers $a_i$, not all zero, with $|a_i|\le k-1$ and $|\sum a_ix_i|\le (k-1)\sqrt n/(k^n-1)$.
solutions_markdown:
Consider the $k^n$ sums $\sum b_i|x_i|$ for integer choices $0\le b_i\le k-1$. All lie in $[0,(k-1)\sum|x_i|]$, an interval of length at most $(k-1)\sqrt n$ by Cauchy–Schwarz.

If two sums coincide, subtract their distinct coefficient vectors to obtain a nonzero vector with dot product zero. Otherwise sort all sums increasingly. The $k^n-1$ consecutive gaps have total at most $(k-1)\sqrt n$, so one gap is at most $(k-1)\sqrt n/(k^n-1)$. Subtract the two coefficient vectors giving that gap. Their entries have absolute value at most $k-1$ and are not all zero. Finally reverse the sign of the corresponding coefficient wherever $x_i<0$ to replace $|x_i|$ by $x_i$.
